hypothesis: Ranking the served crypto basket by ~60-day trailing return and holding the top 3 names ONLY while each clears a positive absolute-momentum gate (else cash) earns more than a fully-invested rotation net of costs and respects the 25% drawdown mandate, because absolute momentum moves the book to cash in broad downtrends; it is false if the gated top-3 underperforms buy-and-hold or breaches 25% drawdown in the 2026 forward window.
origin: Gary Antonacci's dual momentum (relative strength to pick, absolute momentum to gate to cash) applied to the crypto basket, with the cross-sectional/time-series momentum premium documented for crypto by Liu, Tsyvinski & Wu. Distinct from the four-module BULL breakout entry this lab already refuted: that was a single-asset intraday high-breakout rule; this is a monthly portfolio rotation whose drawdown control is the cash switch, not a stop.

hypothesis: Holding each served crypto asset long only while its own price is above its 50-day average, entered at a size inversely proportional to its recent realized volatility and exited on trend loss or a 20% trailing stop, earns multi-week directional moves that clear costs; it is false if the trend-filtered, vol-sized book fails to beat +5.05% in the 2026 forward window or breaches the 25% drawdown mandate.
origin: My own reasoning from this laboratory's record — the two documented intraday failure modes are 25%-drawdown breaches (too much exposure) and 'the book stood still' / too-few-trades (too little). A trend filter that sizes by inverse volatility de-risks BEFORE the mandate and only holds during directional episodes, sitting between those two walls. It is deliberately distinct from the refuted cross-sectional `dual-momentum-rotation`: this is per-asset time-series momentum (each name judged against its own trend, never ranked against the basket), which the crypto-momentum literature reports beats

hypothesis: A long-only 20-day Donchian breakout, taken only while price sits above its 50-day trend and the breakout bar shows above-average volume and then ridden with a 5x-ATR trailing stop, earns positively-skewed returns in crypto because new multi-week highs persist; it is false if these confirmed breakouts do not, on average, run far enough past the 0.30% round-trip cost to pay for the many small trailing-stop losses.
origin: Time-series momentum (Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen 2012) and the classic Turtle/Donchian 20/10 breakout, adapted to 24/7 crypto 5-minute bars. Distinct from the existing quantlab_intraday opening-range momentum: this is a swing breakout that holds for weeks, not an intraday scalp. The lab's own intraday record shows the two failure modes I designed against — repeated 25% drawdown breaches (over-sized) and 'the book stood still' at ~1% exposure (too passive); volatility-targeted sizing with a hard trailing exit sits between them.
